# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart with an unspecified abnormality.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, with issues latching on and spitting up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences frequent falls, even when walking, and has delayed speech.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had recurring issues with fluid in her ear and has experienced speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech and may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech and experiences frequent falls.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may experience developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience short fingers and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor weak enamel and large front teeth
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for structural heart abnormalities
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor for spinal and hip abnormalities
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and learning difficulties
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness and shortness of breath after simple tasks, indicating potential respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other children her age and is often out of breath, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, trouble swallowing certain textures, and often coughs when eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach milestones like walking or sitting compared to other kids, indicating a developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty hearing and tends to turn the volume of the TV very high to hear it properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia and needs glasses to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip easily, requiring frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech and communication issues may impact her educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech and communication difficulties, which may be related to developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to assess cardiac health.
* Speech therapy to address communication difficulties.
* Occupational therapy to support developmental delays and daily functioning.
* Physiotherapy to support motor skills development.
* Behavioural therapy to address any behavioural concerns.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than what is expected for a child of her age and activity level during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight at a slower rate compared to her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than her peers, possibly due to coordination issues, and sometimes struggles to express herself in a way that others understand.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble filtering out background noise or focusing on voices, often asking for repetition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects her ability to see distant objects clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip very easily, requiring frequent dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's myopia may impact her ability to see distant objects clearly in a classroom setting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes struggles to express herself in a way that others understand, making communication challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any issues promptly.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for any hearing loss or difficulties.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any issues such as myopia.
* Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to assess heart health.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any challenges.
* Regular monitoring of the patient's coordination and communication skills to address any emerging issues.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition that requires regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, with trouble latching on and keeping food down, but this has mostly resolved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including being slower to sit up and walk, and has trouble with communication, struggling to make himself understood and getting frustrated when he can't express what he wants.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, with parents often having to repeat themselves, and may have an issue with his hearing that needs to be addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means his eyes get tired easily and he has trouble seeing things clearly, and has trouble wearing his glasses consistently.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to have regular dental check-ups to monitor his teeth and prevent more serious problems later on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and trouble with communication, and gets frustrated when he can't express what he wants.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent more serious problems later on.
* Regular hearing reviews to address the patient's hearing difficulties.
* Regular vision checks to monitor the patient's hypermetropia and ensure consistent use of glasses.
* Regular cardiac check-ups to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's communication difficulties.
* Consideration of occupational therapy and physiotherapy to support the patient's developmental delays.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing or running around, which may be a concern that needs to be monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, which may indicate a need for close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky with food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods due to their texture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which has been a challenge to manage, including finding the right medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond when called, which may not be due to hearing loss but rather inattention or focus on other activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her daily life, such as reading or watching TV, and requires special glasses to correct.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful eating and thorough but gentle brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach milestones than expected, including emotional maturity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach milestones than expected, including emotional maturity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chips or breaks.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and manage symptoms.
* Regular monitoring and management of epilepsy to prevent seizures and find effective medication.
